clue.text: Indulges — if wife gives permission!

parts.note: to allow is to give permission

explanation.surface: A husband pampers himself, but only once his wife has said yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallow in something is to indulge oneself in it with abandon.

clue.text: Tailgated dangerously without learner being worried

indicators.note: driving dangerously suggests chaos, so the letters are thrown about
without signals that the learner's letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: L is the learner sign on cars

explanation.surface: A driver who tailgated recklessly with no learner aboard was left anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dangerously' with 'without' says: take L out of TAILGATED and rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means troubled and anxious, a synonym for worried.

clue.text: Rallies planned to recruit born politicians

indicators.note: recruiting someone takes them into the group, so one piece goes inside another
planned suggests arranged, so the letters of rallies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Organised rallies are set up to draw in natural-born politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges RALLIES into LIERALS, and 'to recruit' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberals are members of a Liberal party, so they are an example of politicians.

clue.text: It's all over!

parts.note: reads as a cry that something has ended, but means something covers every part of a room

explanation.surface: A cry announcing that the match or affair is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall-to-wall describes carpet or coverage that fills the entire space, so it is everywhere.

clue.text: Mean ones to keep identity withheld?

indicators.note: the words keep the answer inside them, spread across both

explanation.surface: Mean people prefer to keep their names secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, the label used when an author's name is unknown or withheld.

clue.text: One saying nothing about parking charge

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: one word about another goes around it

parts.note: someone mute says nothing
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver keeps silent about a parking fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute a fault to someone, as in charging them with it.

clue.text: Artificial fibre seen in a church gallery

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A synthetic textile is on show in a church that doubles as a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a man-made fibre made from cellulose, an example of a synthetic material.

clue.text: Loving look of forest clearing, still timeless

parts.note: a glade is an open space in a forest

indicators.note: losing its time means T, the abbreviation for time, is removed

parts.note: yet means still, as in yet more

explanation.surface: An amorous gaze in a woodland glade, still and outside time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' takes T out of YET, leaving YE.
explanation.definitionFit: The glad eye is an amorous or flirtatious glance, a loving look.

clue.text: Ridiculous claim by one area of the UK that's hostile

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurdly disordered, so the letters of claim are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regional assembly makes an absurd claim that reads as unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical describes an attitude or influence that is unfriendly or harmful, the same as hostile.

clue.text: Horse beginning to panic — that is plain

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, taken here from panic

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: A horse starts to panic, and the cause, it seems, is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' reads as a noun for open country, but it is the adjective, as in a bald statement of fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with patches of black and white, so it is an example of the animal.

clue.text: Inappropriate team from Manchester holding us back

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it within its letters

parts.note: Manchester United, commonly just United, is the football club

indicators.note: going back means the word us is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A football club is ill-suited to the task of keeping us at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team from Manchester' could be City, but only United has room to hold the reversed pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuited means not fitting or appropriate for something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Friend supporting a Parisienne queen in a biased way

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath

parts.note: une is French for a, feminine, as a Parisian woman would say
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend props up a Parisian woman and a queen, though unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequally means unevenly or unfairly, as when treatment is biased.

clue.text: Repeat incentive to replace Conservative by pressure

indicators.note: one letter is swapped for another, with pressure taking the place of Conservative

parts.note: a carrot is an incentive, as in carrot and stick
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Political advice: say it again, and swap the Tory carrot for the stick of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: Bet on yield varying as instructed

indicators.note: letters that vary change their order, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler places a bet on a yield that fluctuates, following orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To act obediently is to do exactly what one is told, as one was instructed.

clue.text: One examines fake requisition when drug goes missing

indicators.note: a fake is not genuine, so the letters of requisition are scrambled
the drug's letter is lost from the mix before rearranging

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A forged order form is noticed when some narcotics vanish from stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' with 'goes missing' says: drop E from REQUISITION and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquisitor questions or investigates people closely, someone who examines.

clue.text: Disheartened revolutionary's dance?

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: a rebel is a revolutionary; the 's means 'is' and links to the definition

explanation.surface: A rebel, crushed by defeat, wonders whether to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes B, the middle letter of REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish folk dance.

clue.text: Standing question over current situation

parts.note: status means social standing
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone's social standing is questioned over how things stand now.
explanation.definitionFit: The status quo is the existing state of affairs, Latin for the state in which.

clue.text: Chances covering international match will be quirks

indicators.note: one word covering another wraps around it

parts.note: odds are chances or probabilities
a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Betting odds on an international match will throw up some oddities.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddities are peculiar traits, the same as quirks.

clue.text: Fellow player possibly met twice with AA

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the word met written out two times, followed by the two letters AA, gives the pool of letters

explanation.surface: Two players may have met at an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MET written twice plus AA. AA looks like Alcoholics Anonymous or the Automobile Association, but here it is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate plays on the same side, a fellow player.

clue.text: Language of bridge is hard

parts.note: to span is to bridge, and a span is a bridge section
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The vocabulary of bridge, the card game, is tough to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish is the language of Spain and much of Latin America.

clue.text: Do a runner from second complainant

parts.note: a carper is someone who carps or complains

explanation.surface: A second person lodging a complaint takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do a runner' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarper is British slang for running away, the same as doing a runner.

clue.text: Expected tense performers

parts.note: something due is expected
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Nervous performers are waiting for their turn on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a pair of musicians or singers, so it can stand for performers.

clue.text: Relish hearing of choice — a flower

indicators.note: what is heard is what is said aloud, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: a pick is a choice, then a, then lily, a flower: said together as one phrase

explanation.surface: A florist enjoys hearing a customer choose a single bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK A LILY spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a mustard-yellow pickle of chopped vegetables, a relish served as a condiment.

clue.text: Helps when cover for broadcast is held

indicators.note: one piece is held by another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: broadcasting sends a word out as speech, so it is taken by its sound

parts.note: a veil is a cover for the face

explanation.surface: Something helps when protection for a broadcast is in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' standing for AS is a common crossword equivalence, as in 'as the clock struck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avails means benefits or is of use to, as in to no avail, so it helps.

clue.text: General manager must be in — it's a terrible shame

indicators.note: the manager must go inside the rest of the letters
something terrible is a mess, so the letters of it's a are scrambled

explanation.surface: Staff are told the general manager has to be in: what a dreadful disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of 'it's a' to STIA before the manager is placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone, a kind of shame.

clue.text: City incorporating weirdly random part of France

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body of another

parts.note: NY is New York City

indicators.note: weirdly signals that the letters of random are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A city that oddly takes in a random piece of French territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weirdly' rearranges the clue's own word into NORMAD; New York is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region of northern France on the English Channel.

clue.text: University administrator may find source of agreement in study

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A college official seeks the origin of a deal by looking in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean heads a faculty or college, an administrator at a university.

clue.text: The new island state with moral values

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so the letters of the are rearranged

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A newly founded island nation built on principled values.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct follows moral principles, the sense of having moral values.

clue.text: The girl would look a day for such a large amount

parts.note: she'd is short for she would, the girl being she
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A girl would give a day a quick look for such a huge sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A shedload is informal British slang for a great quantity of something.

clue.text: Gamble, eating most of dodgy cut of meat

indicators.note: a word eating another takes it inside

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: risky means dodgy or hazardous

explanation.surface: A wager at a butcher's that consumes most of some questionable joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final Y from the synonym for dodgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is beef from the breast of the animal, a cut used for slow cooking.
